column3: The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the priest” and introduces the healed condition with “behold”; BSB names the priest once and introduces it with “if.”
After the priest’s command, the Hebrew uses an active singular taking verb; BSB makes the supplies the subject of passive “be brought.”
The Hebrew calls the water “living water”; BSB says “fresh water.”
The Hebrew names “the live bird” twice and calls the water “living water”; BSB names the bird once and says “fresh water.”
The Hebrew locates the release “over the face of the field”; BSB says “into the open field.”
The Hebrew says he will be “clean,” without an explicit word “ceremonially”; BSB adds that qualifier.
The Hebrew repeats “all his hair” and the shaving verb; BSB uses “the rest of his hair” for the second occurrence. It also says to wash “his flesh,” rendered as bathing “himself” in BSB.
The Hebrew calls the ewe “a daughter of her year” and names three tenth-measures without explicitly naming an ephah. It says “oil” twice; BSB specifies “olive oil” both times.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “oil”; BSB specifies “olive oil.”
The Hebrew uses active “he slaughters” for the customary sacrifices; BSB uses passive “are slaughtered.” It also renders “holiness of holinesses” as “most holy.”
The Hebrew repeats “the priest” for taking and applying the blood; BSB states the subject once.
The Hebrew repeats “the priest” in “the priest’s left palm” and says “oil”; BSB uses “his left palm” and specifies “olive oil.”
The Hebrew says “his right finger”; BSB specifies “his right forefinger.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew gives atonement as another finite action and repeats “the priest”; BSB expresses it as a purpose with “to make atonement.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names the burnt offering and repeats “the priest” twice; BSB uses “it” and continues the preceding subject without repeating the title.
The Hebrew expresses inability as “his hand does not reach,” and says “oil”; BSB says “cannot afford these offerings” and specifies “olive oil.”
The Hebrew calls the young pigeons “sons of a dove” and expresses affordability as what “his hand reaches”; BSB says “young pigeons” and “he can afford.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the priest” for taking and waving and says “oil”; BSB names the priest once and specifies “olive oil.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the priest” in the palm description; BSB says “his left palm.”
The Hebrew says “his right finger”; BSB specifies “his right forefinger.”
The Hebrew names singular “the place of the blood”; BSB says plural “the same places as the blood.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says “the one from the turtledoves or from the sons of the dove”; BSB gives plural “the turtledoves or young pigeons.”
